content.text: {"relation":"MATCH","consensus_summary":"The blind consensus offers two dominant strands: (1) the tail as the false prophet / teacher of lies, resting on Isaiah 9:15's explicit self-definition and extended to the dragon's tail (Rev 12:4) and demonic tails (Rev 9:10,19) as deceptive/destructive satanic influence; (2) the tail as subordination or last place versus the head (Deut 28:13,44). Responses A and C make the false-prophet reading primary; B and D make the head/tail status contrast primary, with false prophecy as a common alternative. Most responses judge there is no single settled meaning and that context decides between these two recognized strands.","book_summary":"The book identifies the tail as 'the prophet that teacheth lies,' citing Isaiah's own explicit decode, and grounds the head/tail polarity in the Deuteronomy 28 covenant blessing and curse. It reads Revelation 12:4 as the led being destroyed by the misleading (echoing Isa 9:16), Revelation 9:19's serpent-tails that 'had heads' as the liar enthroned, and Exodus 4:4 (Moses seizing the serpent by the tail) as symbolically apt.","consensus_core_identification":"Tail = falsehood/false prophecy (the lying prophet, per Isaiah 9:15) and/or the subordinate, inferior position opposite the head (per Deut 28); the false-prophet sense is the explicitly scripture-defined symbol and is primary in half the responses and listed as common in all.","book_core_identification":"Tail = the prophet that teaches lies — deceptive false leadership — with the covenant head/tail contrast (Deut 28) supplying the underlying frame, and Revelation's tail imagery read as deception destroying those it leads.","core_relation":"EQUIVALENT","extension_relation":"SAME_CASES","boundary_disagreement":"Minimal. The book fuses the two consensus strands rather than choosing between them: the Deut 28 head/tail status contrast is treated as the covenant backdrop that Isaiah then decodes as lying prophecy, whereas some consensus responses treat status and false prophecy as separate, context-dependent meanings. The book also reads Exodus 4:4 symbolically (seizing the serpent at the tail = at the point of the lie), which one consensus minority strand explicitly classified as merely literal narrative — a small case reclassification, not a boundary shift in the central identification.","material_contradiction":"None. The book's identification is the same explicitly scripture-defined meaning (Isa 9:15) that two of four consensus responses make primary and all four list as a well-recognized reading; its Revelation readings track the consensus's deception/destructive-influence interpretations.","rationale":"The book's core — tail as the lying prophet, per Isaiah's own equation, with Deut 28 defining the head/tail polarity and Revelation's tails as deception's destructive sweep — is directly covered by the consensus's leading strand (primary in Responses A and C, common alternative in B and D). Since the consensus itself acknowledges two mainstream strands and the book affirms both while making the Isaiah decode central, this is agreement in wording and emphasis, not a changed extension or replaced referent. The only extra move, treating Exodus 4:4 as symbolically significant, is immaterial detail relative to the core identification.","citation_support":"STRONG","strongest_objection":"One could argue REFINED because the book subordinates the Deut 28 status meaning under the false-prophecy meaning (making one unified symbol rather than two context-dependent ones) and reclassifies Exodus 4:4 from literal narrative to symbolic instance, slightly broadening the symbol's coverage against the consensus minority caution that not all tail texts are symbolic.","confidence":"high"}
